This revision has been filed challenging the order dated 07.01.2020 passed by Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Basti in Criminal Appeal No. 38 of 2021 (Pankaj through his father Ram Autar Vs. State) as well as judgement and order dated 07.01.2022 passed by Juvenile Justice Board, Basti regarding bail in Case Crime No.- 142 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and 5/6 POCSO Act, P.S.- Walterganj, District- Basti.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the revisionist that revisionist is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is submitted that first information report has been lodged by father of victim against four accused persons with the allegation that they enticed the minor daughter of informant.
The revisionist was not named in the first information report.
The statement of victim was recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and in both the statements there is no allegation of rape against the revisionist.
The Investigating Officer after recording the majid statement of victim has submitted charge sheet under Section 376 I.P.C.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the revisionist that since the victim has not levelled any allegation of rape against the revisionist in her statement under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., there is no offence under Section 376 is made out against the revisionist.
The revisionist is in juvenile home since 17.06.2021.
There is no other criminal history of revisionist.

Learned counsel for the revisionist further argues that admittedly, the revisionist is a juvenile and while deciding the bail application, the Juvenile Justice Board has solely considered the gravity of the offence alleged and had not even considered the requirement of the proviso to Section 12(1) of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection) Act, 2015 (in short 'the Act').
He argues that the Appellate Court had committed the same error in dismissing the appeal.
Learned AGA vehemently opposed the prayer for bail but did not dispute the aforesaid facts.
I have perused the orders that reject the bail application and the appeal, which do not record any reasons as required in terms of the proviso to Section 12(1) of the Act.
Considering the age of the revisionist who is minor and in custody since 17.06.2021, the revision deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, the revision is allowed and the impugned judgement and orders dated 30.10.2021 and 07.01.2022 are set aside.
The bail application of the revisionist is also allowed.

Let the revisionist Pankaj be released on bail in the aforementioned case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of Chief Judicial Magistrate/Juvenile Justice Board concerned.

Order Date :- 21.7.2023 Virendra  Pankaj vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48997607/
